newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks open higher in cautious rebound.
newsitem.headline: French stocks open higher in cautious rebound.

text.p: French stocks rebounded in early trade on Wednesday on higher bond prices and a firm franc.

Traders said the bourse's gains were likely to be limited during a two-day meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee. No announcement from the meeting begun on Tuesday was expected before late on Wednesday.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 13.35 points, or 0.53 percent, at 2,516.42 at 0930 GMT, within striking distance of its all time high of 2,521.88. The CAC-40 February futures contract was 14 points higher at 2,524.
Volume in the first 40 minutes of trade was 1.1 billion francs, with interest centred on companies issuing results.
Skis Rossignol shares shot up 6.39 percent to 161.60 francs after the sports equipment maker reported an 11.4 percent rise in nine-month sales.
Skincare firm Clarins' shares rose 3.41 percent to 788 francs after it reported a 15.8 percent rise in 1996 sales and forecast double-digit profit growth for 1996.
Retailer Carrefour's stock was 2.97 percent higher at 3,359 francs after the group reported a 10.5 percent rise in January sales.
